issues.description: download_and_untar.sh reports missing unzip but does not exit, letting the script proceed and fail later
issues.detail: The unzip check prints a message and falls through. Missing-tool detection and continued execution are complected: one branch is supposed to be a precondition, the other is the happy path. Simple fix: exit non-zero when unzip is absent. Right now the failure mode is a confusing downstream error instead of a clear precondition violation.

issues.description: Argument-count error path prints usage but does not exit, masking a misuse as success
issues.detail: When fewer than 1 or more than 2 args are passed, the script prints usage and continues into realpath of an unset $1. The control-flow concept (validate, then proceed) is complected with the documentation concept (here-doc help). Adding exit 1 after the usage block separates the two and surfaces misuse immediately rather than as a cryptic realpath failure.

issues.description: Three near-identical zip-extraction blocks duplicate the same value (archive name, target dir, sentinel) inline
issues.detail: TAL_ASR-1/2/3 each get a hand-rolled if/elif/else with the same shape. The essential data is a small table of (zip_name, target_subdir); the incidental complexity is repeating the control flow three times. A single loop over that table would make adding a fourth archive a one-line data change instead of a 10-line copy. Classic easy-not-simple: cut-and-paste was near at hand, decomposition was not.

issues.description: data.sh hardcodes expected utterance counts inline with partition definitions, complecting validation with configuration
issues.detail: The here-doc mixes partition layout (name, wav dir, transcript) with a per-partition integrity check (num_wav). The integrity check is a fact about a specific dataset snapshot; the partition layout is a fact about the recipe. Entangling them means any upstream count change forces a recipe edit. Pull the expected counts into a separate validation step or out entirely; let the recipe describe partitions, not assert dataset versions.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is a chain of inline seds that hides the actual character map
issues.detail: Five sed substitutions in a pipe encode a normalization policy (full-width to half-width A, strip punctuation). The policy is data: a list of (from, to) pairs. Right now the data is dissolved into shell syntax, so adding or auditing a rule means reading a pipeline. A small replacement table read by one sed -f would make the rule set a value you can inspect, version, and reuse.

issues.description: README ASR config link points to a path (conf/train/...) that does not match the actual file location (conf/...)
issues.detail: The link reads ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml but the file lives at conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. Small incidental error, but the README is the artifact a future reader trusts to navigate the recipe; a broken value here is a small instance of the larger problem of facts about the code drifting from the code.

review.summary: This is a recipe-addition PR that mostly composes existing ESPnet templates via symlinks and YAML, which is the right shape — values and configuration as data, not new control flow. The novel code is the two shell scripts (download_and_untar.sh and local/data.sh), and that is where complecting shows up: error handling tangled with happy paths, repeated extraction blocks that should be a small data table looped over, and dataset-version assertions braided into partition definitions. None of the issues are correctness time-bombs at training time, but they are the kind of "easy" choices that will calcify into incidental complexity the next time someone adds a partition or a new archive. The README link drift is a small but characteristic symptom: the description of the artifact and the artifact have already begun to disagree.
